extra_sources.quote: “average lot size” in this case refers to the total residential area developed divided by the total number of residential units in each county, including multi-family units. It should not be interpreted as the average lot size for single family homes only.
extra_sources.locator: Section 4, text immediately above Table 4-9 (PDF p.45)

arithmetic: Independent inputs: 1.2M households (Gardner 2025) x 0.86 basin share (UPC 2025, see share_in_basin) x 0.72 = 743,040. Model chain: 3.65M implied pop / 2.83 x 0.80 x 0.72 = 743k. Same result: the model's low share (0.80) and low household size (2.83) offset each other.
notes: RESOLVES findings.md lawn discrepancy: Table 4-9's landscaped area (Salt Lake 4,239 etc.) is per residential UNIT including multifamily, so it must be multiplied by ALL basin households (~1.02-1.03M), not by the 72% 'with a lawn'. Population-weighted (UPC 2025) landscaped area per unit for the 12 basin counties = 5,789 sq ft; 1.02M units x 5,789 = ~136,000 landscaped acres (model: 743k x 6,938 = 118,000). Then 408.5 KAF -> 36 in/yr and 371 KAF -> 33 in/yr, both plausible (Table 4-7: JVWCD homeowner average applied 50 in; statewide irrigation efficiency ~63%). So the fix is to pair the published per-unit area with all households (or keep 743k for compliance counts but use 5,789 sq ft x ~1.02M units for acreage). 0.72 share_with_lawn remains an assumption.
